name: Silver Nova
lede: Silversea’s Silver Nova was designed to bring guests closer to their destination. Seventy Platinum Electric Marine heaters, recessed or suspended, warm its main gathering spaces without drawing the eye from the view.

hero.caption: Platinum Electric Marine on the beam of a ship-top terrace. Bromic-published photograph from the case study.

photos.caption: A deck lounge under the glazed canopy. Bromic-published photograph from the case study.
White heaters flush in a promenade ceiling. Bromic-published photograph from the case study.

beats: The twelfth ship in Silversea’s fleet carries up to 728 guests. Its asymmetrical, horizontal design links public areas in one continuous flow, and aft suites have 270° views.
The Royal Caribbean Group’s designers wanted comfortable warmth in outdoor and gathering areas that stayed visually unobtrusive and supported year-round use.

Working with Bromic’s Daniel Bruntsch on a free 2D heat plan, the team placed 70 Platinum Smart-Heat Electric Marine heaters, with recess kits and mounting poles for flush and suspended installs. Meyer Werft installed them in Papenburg, Germany.
